name: Kingdom of Aksum
summary: A northeastern African state linking the Ethiopian and Eritrean highlands with Red Sea commerce and, at times, southern Arabia.
currency: Gold, silver, and copper coinage; minting began in the late third century.
economy: Agriculture and commerce through Red Sea connections supported the kingdom.
military: Royal campaigns extended power beyond the highlands, including into southern Arabia at its height.
contributions: Monumental stelae, distinctive architecture and coinage, and an enduring written and Christian cultural legacy.
origin: An urban trading and political centre developed in the northern Ethiopian highlands during the early first millennium.
decline: Changing Red Sea trade and environmental pressures contributed to political and economic reorganization; the process was gradual and remains debated.
